status: Usage levels approved by the user (October 9, 2026). Time-of-use shares and seasons copied from official OEB sources; null where no official share is published. Reference-customer conditions (conditional charges the typical customer of a sector pays) added October 9, 2026 per the user's decision to include a reviewed list. A SYNTHETIC business-hours load profile ('synthetic_profiles') was added October 16, 2026 (user-approved) for the Phase 7E illustrative estimate only; it never changes a model's own numbers.   Reference-customer rules for fixed charges published as phase or amperage variants ('fixed_charge_variants') added October 30, 2026 (user decision). Historical market benchmarks ('market_benchmarks') approved November 2, 2026: 60 equal-weight monthly arithmetic prices, Ontario with Class B GA and Alberta pool energy only, maximum window lag four months. These are separate from base medians and synthetic estimates, not customer-weighted bills. Method 7D-2 (owner decisions November 20, 2026): commercial gas levels for small and mid-size buildings, the s1/s2 small-business levels at 14 and 40 kW, documented backing for every level, Liberty Gas NB's peak-month factor and customer-charge rules, Energir's basic-fee band rule, and reference-customer entries for Energir's load balancing and renewable-gas socialization charges and Liberty Utility Gas. Method 7T-1 (owner decisions November 24, 2026): the territorial models reuse the residential and s1/s2 levels unchanged; each of those levels carries its northern reference points ('north', decision 73), and the NWT TPSP seasonal first block is month-weighted (seasons NT_TPSP, decision 68).

gas.note: Phase 7D (owner decisions 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-20): default utility supply priced in each utility's native billing unit. Residential levels since 7D-1; commercial general-service levels for two building sizes since 7D-2, each with a reference level and x0.5 and x2 sensitivity levels. A level is an average month: annual use = 12 x the level, which selects each utility's class (published annual limits) unless a peak_month_factors entry applies. The m3 and GJ tracks are never converted or merged; a future cross-unit comparison converts toward m3, with its heating-value source chosen then. Contract-demand, interruptible, seasonal and peaking classes are not modelled yet (owner decision 2026-11-20).

NT_TPSP.method: GNWT Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP) first block in the after-subsidy cost: compute each usage level's cost once per season with that season's first block at the stored Yellowknife-rate price, which is all-in (it replaces the whole per-kWh price of the first-block kWh, riders and credits included: owner decisions 76 and 78), then month-weight: cost = (7 x September-March + 5 x April-August) / 12, as for Ontario's RPP tiers (ON_RPP). The engine checks every stored first-block threshold against first_block_kwh_per_month; a different threshold or months that do not cover the year once make the after-subsidy cost not computable.

source.title: Northwest Territories Power Corporation, Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP)
source.quote: From September 1 to March 31 each year, residential customers only pay the Yellowknife rate on the first 1,000 kilowatt hours (kWh) of power that they consume. After 1,000 kWh, each additional kilowatt hour is charged at the Zone Rate. From April 1 to August 31 – when there are more hours of daylight – residential customers pay the Yellowknife rate (where costs are lower) on the first 600 kilowatt hours -- after that, each additional kilowatt hour, is charged at the Zone Rate.
source.cross_check: Naka Power Utilities (NWT) Rate Schedule effective July 1, 2026, Territorial Power Subsidy Program (TPSP), PDF page 32 (https://www.nakapower.com/content/dam/web/nakapower/2026-07-01-NPUNWT-rate-schedule.pdf): 'The Territorial Support is limited to 1000 kW.h per month during September to March and 600 kW.h per month during April to August, pro-rated on a 30 day charge period basis.'
source.note: The block is applied per average month (1,000 or 600 kWh), as decided; Naka's pro-rating on a 30-day charge period is not modelled.

reference_customer_basis: Conditional components are left out of modeled costs unless an entry below says that the reference (typical) customer of the sector pays them (user decision, October 9, 2026). An entry applies to components of its province and fuel, for the listed sectors (residential or a commercial size band), whose notes (after the 'Provenance: ...' prefix) fully match notes_regex and whose component name fully matches name_regex (Python re.fullmatch; every given pattern must match). Only components otherwise excluded as 'conditional' qualify: alternatives, optional components, expired or not-yet-effective components and value-less market components stay excluded. Included components are itemized with reason 'reference_customer:<id>'. Ontario reference customers: residential and GS < 50 kW customers are on the Regulated Price Plan (RPP) and buy from their distributor (standard supply); customers at the 50 kW and over levels buy spot-priced energy through their distributor (non-RPP standard supply); all are Class B (not Industrial Conservation Initiative participants) and none is a wholesale market participant. Still excluded: the Hydro One RRRP credit (principal-residence condition), EV charging rates, former Chapleau PUC rider sets, transformer-ownership allowances, primary-metering and transformer-loss allowances, and meter-type, interval-meter and demand-size alternatives.

fixed_charge_variants_basis: A fixed charge published as variants of one charge, either as unconditional variants such as 'Basic Customer Charge (Single Phase)' / 'Basic Customer Charge (Three Phase)', as alternatives marked 'Alternative: applies ...', or as bands of annual volume of which one applies, is priced for the reference customer of the usage level. Rules select by level (user decision, October 30, 2026: homes are single-phase service of 200 A; small businesses are single-phase at s1 and three-phase at s2, now 14 kW and 40 kW, owner decision 2026-11-20), by the level's monthly peak (a 'peak_month' range tested on the level x its peak_month_factors entry: Liberty Gas NB customer charges, owner decision 17, 2026-11-20) or by annual-volume band ('select': 'annual_volume_band': the band whose published annual window strictly contains 12 x the level; Energir's basic fee per metering device, owner decision 8, 2026-11-20). A rule applies to its fuel, sectors and, when given, province, utility and tariff_code; the variant whose component name fully matches match.name_regex (Python re.fullmatch) is priced. Exactly one matching variant with a value per month is priced and itemized with reason 'fixed_charge_variant:<id>'; no match or more than one leaves the record not computable at that level with the existing reason.

peak_month_factors_basis: Some classes and charges follow a customer's monthly peak rather than its average month. An entry gives the ratio of the peak month to the average month for a province, fuel and sectors; the engine multiplies the level by it wherever a crosswalk usage_bounds entry (basis 'peak_month') or a fixed_charge_variants 'peak_month' rule applies.

peak_month_factors.basis: Liberty Gas NB places a customer in Mid-General Service (under 250 GJ) or Large General Service (250 GJ and over) by its 'Monthly Demand Peak' over the last 12 months, and its customer charges change at 60 GJ (MGS) and 650 GJ (LGS) of maximum monthly consumption. The peak month of an average-month level is taken as January: New Brunswick's commercial and institutional customers used 1.85 times their average month in January 2025. Liberty's own 2024 class data give about 2.0 (MGS) and 1.7 (LGS).

basis: Monthly usage levels: electricity residential 500/1,000/2,000 kWh (approved October 9, 2026; 1,000 kWh is the reference level and 500/2,000 are sensitivity levels, owner decision November 20, 2026); commercial under 50 kW s1 = 2,000 kWh at 14 kW and s2 = 10,000 kWh at 40 kW (owner decision November 20, 2026, replacing 2,000 kWh at 10 kW and 8,000 kWh at 25 kW); 50-499 kW m1 = 40,000 kWh at 100 kW; 500-4,999 kW l1 = 500,000 kWh at 1,000 kW; no level yet for 5,000 kW and over. Gas levels are in the gas section (native m3 or GJ, residential and commercial). Each level records its decision, what it represents, why it was chosen and its sources (owner rule November 20, 2026). Daily charges convert to monthly at 30.4375 days (365.25 / 12); hours per month 730.5. kVA demand is derived from kW at the disclosed 0.9 power factor (kVA = kW / 0.9) and never treated as kW. Implied load factors (kWh / (kW x 730.5)): s1 19.6%, s2 34.2%, m1 54.8%, l1 68.4%. Levels are comparison points for modeled costs, not a load profile of any customer.
